expectations.text: Models the subscription as a first-class stateful object with full CRUD rather than fire-and-forget registration.
expectations.evidence: Subscription object JSON and the endpoints table (POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE).

expectations.text: Specifies three explicit states: active, paused, and disabled.
expectations.evidence: 'status has three values.'

expectations.text: Defines paused as subscriber-initiated and disabled as platform-initiated after sustained failure.
expectations.evidence: 'active and paused can be set by the customer. disabled is platform-only'.

expectations.text: Answers the maintenance-window question with the paused state, not with delete-and-recreate and not with the existing enabled: false flag.
expectations.evidence: 'The customer pauses the subscription before the window, or sets paused_until.'

expectations.text: Flags delete-and-recreate as destroying the subscription's replay and delivery-tracking state.
expectations.evidence: 'Deleting destroys the subscription's delivery and replay state.'

expectations.text: Warns that recreating a subscription under the same name restarts from the default position, so the subscriber silently loses or double-replays a backlog.
expectations.evidence: 'The new subscription starts at "new events only", so every stuck event is either silently lost or double-replayed.'

expectations.text: Specifies two independently configured replay positions: where a newly created subscription starts, and where a subscription resumes after a platform-side incident.
expectations.evidence: replay: on_create 'latest', on_resume 'earliest_undelivered'.

expectations.text: States that those two replay positions can legitimately differ, and that both must be specified.
expectations.evidence: 'The two positions are configured separately, as the skill's lifecycle section requires.'

expectations.text: Says to expose only the states a customer-created subscription may legally reach, rejecting internal-only states at the API boundary.
expectations.evidence: 'disabled is platform-only and is rejected on write.'

expectations.text: Keeps the two filtering axes independent: event type selected against the catalog, and recipient or channel scoping.
expectations.evidence: 'scope is a second filter, independent of event_types.'

expectations.text: States that an endpoint with no filter configured receives everything, and that this must be documented explicitly.
expectations.evidence: 'null means all events. Say so in the docs.'

expectations.text: Documents config-change propagation lag, a subscription edit taking a minute or two to reach the delivery path, as expected behavior rather than a bug.
expectations.evidence: Propagation lag is not mentioned.
